_what: Adjudication of every denial edge on the board: which of the three denial states it is, and where the record names an issuer, which end issued it. Keyed by "a|b", the edge's own two ends in the order the record stores them. Read by tools/merge.py, which stamps denialKind and denier onto the edge records.
_why: Until this file existed the renderer inferred direction from [a,b].sort() -- alphabetical order -- and drew an arrowhead on every denial edge. 22 of the 47 on the map pointed the wrong way. build_l0.py recorded the convention as "CONFIRMED against the merged board" on the strength of ONE agreeing sample. notes/DENIAL-DIRECTION-2026-08-26.md.
_method:
All 174 read one at a time, label and note, against a rule fixed BEFORE reading any of them so the rule could not be bent to fit a case:
  directed   - the label names, or unambiguously identifies, the party that issued the denial, AND that party is one of the two ends. `denier` is that end.
  association - the edge is not a denial ACT: a transmission, a naming, a structural or definitional relation, a scholarly dispute, a criticism OF a denial.
  undirected  - it is a denial act, but the issuer is not named or is not one of the two ends. This claims the least and is the correct default; where a reading was arguable it went here rather than to a guessed direction.
_result: 174 adjudicated: 124 directed (90 issued by the `a` end, 34 by the `b` end), 36 association, 14 undirected. THE SHIPPED CONVENTION WAS WRONG ON 34 OF 124 -- 27 per cent. On the 47 edges drawn on the map: 22 `a`, 16 `b`, 5 undirected, 4 association.
_not_a_sourcing_claim: Nothing here adds a fact. Every verdict is a reading of the label and note already on the edge; no new party, date or document is named. Where the existing label was not enough to identify an issuer, the verdict is `undirected` rather than an inference.
